angle: This video isolates the single most-confused distinction on this node by holding one normal curve of mouse weights fixed and flipping which side varies: areas under the curve for probability versus curve height at fixed data for likelihood.
angle_detail: Watch [00:47]–[03:36] straight through, since the 29% area example and the 0.12-versus-0.21 height comparison only land as a pair. It assumes you already read areas as probabilities and points nowhere near maximum likelihood estimation, so use it to fix direction-of-conditioning errors, not to learn fitting. At five minutes there is nothing to skip, but bring a second source for any actual estimator.
